headline: 18 wickets fall as Shoriful Islam takes 6-35 to keep Bangladesh alive
summary: After being bowled out for 64, Shoriful's maiden six-wicket haul prevents a total collapse against Australia in the second Test in Mackay.
details: A chaotic opening day in Mackay saw 18 wickets fall for 229 runs, with Shoriful Islam delivering a stunning comeback for Bangladesh after a disastrous first innings.
Bangladesh were bundled out for just 64 in 34 overs, their fourth-lowest Test total, after Mitchell Starc ripped through the batting order with a six-wicket haul (6-12).

Shoriful Islam, batting at No. 11, top-scored for the Tigers with 14 runs, becoming the first Test cricketer to score the highest runs for his team from No. 11 and then take the most wickets in the opposition's innings.
Turning the game around, Shoriful claimed 6-35 from 11 overs, dismissing key Australian batters including Travis Head, Marnus Labuschagne, and Steven Smith.
Australia reached 165 for eight at stumps on Day 1, holding a lead of 101 runs with Josh Hazlewood still to bat.
The 18-wicket tally on the opening day was the third-highest in Australian Test history since 1975, underlining the extraordinary nature of the day's play.

headline: President Mirza Fakhrul pays tribute to Liberation War martyrs in Savar
summary: The newly elected president laid a floral wreath at the National Martyrs' Memorial and received a state salute from the three armed forces.
details: President Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir visited the National Martyrs' Memorial in Savar today at 10:00 am to honor the martyrs of the Liberation War.
He laid a floral wreath at the altar and stood in solemn silence to mark his respect for those who sacrificed their lives for the country.
A contingent of the three armed forces presented a state salute while the bugle played the Last Post during the ceremony.
The event was attended by State Minister for Liberation War Affairs Ishraque Hossain and the chiefs of the Army, Navy, and Air Force.
After the formal proceedings, President Fakhrul signed the visitors' book and planted a sapling on the memorial premises.
Mirza Fakhrul, formerly the longest-serving second-in-command of the BNP, was sworn in as the President of Bangladesh yesterday.
caption:
President Mirza Fakhrul honors the martyrs of the Liberation War in his first visit to the National Memorial.

President Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir visited the National Martyrs' Memorial in Savar today at 10:00 am to honor the martyrs of the Liberation War.

He laid a floral wreath at the altar and stood in solemn silence to mark his respect for those who sacrificed their lives for the country.

A contingent of the three armed forces presented a state salute while the bugle played the Last Post during the ceremony.

The event was attended by State Minister for Liberation War Affairs Ishraque Hossain and the chiefs of the Army, Navy, and Air Force.

After the formal proceedings, President Fakhrul signed the visitors' book and planted a sapling on the memorial premises.

Mirza Fakhrul, formerly the longest-serving second-in-command of the BNP, was sworn in as the President of Bangladesh yesterday.
